description_good_justification: The README opens with what the package does: a JavaScript function to calculate the angle between two coordinates: https://github.com/phun-ky/angle/blob/main/README.md#about
interact_justification: The README explains how to get the package (npm), use it, give feedback (GitHub issues) and contribute: https://github.com/phun-ky/angle/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_justification: The contribution process (issues, pull requests, checks, sign-off): https://github.com/phun-ky/angle/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-code
contribution_requirements_justification: Contribution requirements, including coding style and tests, are in CONTRIBUTING.md: https://github.com/phun-ky/angle/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-code
documentation_basics_justification: Getting started, usage for ES modules, CommonJS and the browser, and errors and edge cases: https://phun-ky.net/angle/guide/
documentation_interface_justification: The API reference, generated from the source with TypeDoc: https://phun-ky.net/angle/api/functions/angle
sites_https_justification: The repository and the npm package are served over HTTPS: https://github.com/phun-ky/angle
discussion_justification: GitHub issues and pull requests are searchable, addressable by URL and open to anyone with a GitHub account: https://github.com/phun-ky/angle/issues
english_justification: All documentation is in English, and reports and comments in English are accepted.
maintained_justification: The project is actively maintained, with releases and changes in October 2026: https://github.com/phun-ky/angle/releases
repo_track_justification: Git records who changed what and when: https://github.com/phun-ky/angle/commits/main
repo_interim_justification: Every change is a public commit and pull request between releases, not only the releases themselves.
version_unique_justification: Every release has a unique version, tagged as <version>: https://github.com/phun-ky/angle/tags
version_semver_justification: Semantic Versioning; the public API only breaks in a major release: https://github.com/phun-ky/angle/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
version_tags_justification: Each release is tagged in git: https://github.com/phun-ky/angle/tags
release_notes_justification: A CHANGELOG.md generated from conventional commits, also published as GitHub release notes: https://github.com/phun-ky/angle/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: No release has fixed a publicly known vulnerability in the published package. Such a fix would be listed in the release notes and a GitHub security advisory.
report_tracker_justification: Issues are tracked on GitHub: https://github.com/phun-ky/angle/issues
report_responses_justification: Every issue is assigned to the maintainer when it is opened. No one outside the project has filed a bug report in the last 12 months, so none is unanswered.
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests are answered in their GitHub issue. No one outside the project has filed one in the last 12 months, so none is unanswered.
report_archive_justification: All issues and pull requests stay public and searchable on GitHub: https://github.com/phun-ky/angle/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private reports through GitHub private vulnerability reporting or by email: https://github.com/phun-ky/angle/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: Reports are acknowledged within 7 days; no vulnerability has been reported in the last 6 months: https://github.com/phun-ky/angle/blob/main/SECURITY.md#how-reports-are-handled
build_justification: npm run build builds the ES module, CommonJS, UMD and type declarations with rollup: https://github.com/phun-ky/angle/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#development
build_common_tools_justification: npm, rollup and the TypeScript compiler.
build_floss_tools_justification: npm, Node.js, rollup and TypeScript are all FLOSS.
test_justification: A node:test suite, run with npm test, and a packaging check (npm run check:pack) that installs the packed package and calls angle() from every entry point: https://github.com/phun-ky/angle/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
test_invocation_justification: npm test, the standard way to run tests in an npm project.
test_most_justification: The source is at 100% of lines, functions and branches; test:ci fails below 99% of lines, 100% of functions or 95% of branches, and coverage is uploaded to Codecov from every CI run.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: The Checks workflow lints, type-checks, tests, builds and packs every pull request and every push to main: https://github.com/phun-ky/angle/blob/main/.github/workflows/check.yml
test_policy_justification: New functionality must come with tests and bug fixes with a regression test: https://github.com/phun-ky/angle/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
tests_are_added_justification: Recent changes came with tests: the packaging fix in 1.0.65 (#114) came with check:pack, which runs in CI and failed on the broken 1.0.64 package.
tests_documented_added_justification: The tests policy is part of the instructions for contributing code: https://github.com/phun-ky/angle/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
warnings_justification: TypeScript runs in strict mode, ESLint (typescript-eslint, stylistic and Prettier rules) on every file including Markdown, and TypeDoc treats warnings as errors.
warnings_fixed_justification: Lint has no errors and no warnings, TypeScript has no errors, and TypeDoc has no warnings.
warnings_strict_justification: TypeScript runs with strict: true, TypeDoc treats warnings as errors in CI, and lint errors fail the Checks workflow.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer knows how to design secure software. The principles applied: a pure function with no side effects and no dynamic code, one runtime dependency by the same maintainer, declared and never bundled, least-privilege CI tokens, pinned Actions, and releases with provenance. What the package guarantees and does not: https://github.com/phun-ky/angle/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer knows the common errors for this kind of software: injection and dynamic code (none: no eval or code loading), supply chain (one declared runtime dependency by the same maintainer, checked in CI not to be bundled, locked and reviewed development dependencies, pinned Actions), and unchecked input (documented: NaN and Infinity pass through): https://github.com/phun-ky/angle/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
crypto_published_justification: The package implements and calls no cryptography, and does no network access: angle() is a pure function on four numbers. See the security expectations: https://github.com/phun-ky/angle/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
crypto_call_justification: The package implements and calls no cryptography, and does no network access: angle() is a pure function on four numbers. See the security expectations: https://github.com/phun-ky/angle/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations

delivery_mitm_justification: The package is delivered by npm over HTTPS with Sigstore-signed provenance, and the repository by GitHub over HTTPS.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hashes are fetched over HTTP; npm verifies package integrity from the registry metadata over HTTPS.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: The published package has no known vulnerabilities (npm audit --omit=dev runs before every release). Development tooling alerts are fixed or accepted as described in the security policy: https://github.com/phun-ky/angle/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependencies
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerability has been found in the published package.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credentials are in the repository; GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enabled: https://github.com/phun-ky/angle/blob/main/SECURITY.md#secrets
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (GitHub default setup) analyses every pull request and push to main, and ESLint runs on every pull request.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL analyses the JavaScript/TypeScript code and the GitHub Actions workflows on every push to main and every pull request, and the ruleset on main requires its results, with no errors and no high or critical security alerts, before merging: https://github.com/phun-ky/angle/blob/main/SECURITY.md#code-scanning
static_analysis_fixed_justification: CodeQL has no open alerts; the ruleset blocks merging with a high or critical one.
static_analysis_often_justification: On every pull request and every push to main.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No fuzzing or property-based testing yet.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: All software is TypeScript on JavaScript runtimes, which are memory-safe; there is no C, C++ or other memory-unsafe code.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: No run-time assertions beyond the input type checks; stricter input checks are considered for a 2.0 in the roadmap.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis is run yet, so it has found nothing to fix.
